UV spectroscopy and Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) study: | UV spectroscopy was analyzed from the reaction mixture between benzenesulfonamide and chlorobenzene in DMSO at standard conditions. Spectra of Fe(acac)₃, Fe(acac)₂, and CuI in DMSO were recorded to serve as references for comparison. The reaction mixture after 1 h and 15 h showed a peak resembling that of Fe(acac)2 at around 275 nm, which indicates the formation of iron (II) species in the reaction mixture (Figure S4a). Furthermore, the reaction mixture, both after 1 h and 15 h showed another peak similar to CuI at around 270 nm, which suggests the formation of Cu(I) species in the reaction mixture (Figure S4a). Additionally, after one hour of analysis, an additional peak at 305 nm appeared in the reaction mixture. This peak may arise from the formation of another iron intermediate generated during the catalytic cycle.
Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis of the residual powder, collected after extracting the organic compounds, indicated the existence of both Fe(II) and Fe(III) species, along with Cu(I) (Figure S4b). This solid preserved its catalytic efficiency through four consecutive cycles, showing no appreciable decrease in activity (Figure S2).
